ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, D is a point on the extension of side BC of $\triangle ABC$, and $CD=BC$, with line DE intersecting AB and AC at points E and F, respectively. If $EA = EB$, then $\frac{AF}{AC}=?$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct line $EG \parallel BD$ through point $E$, intersecting $AC$ at point $G$,\\
since $AE=BE$ and $BC=CD$,\\
therefore $AB=2AE$,\\
therefore $\triangle AEG \sim \triangle ABC$,\\
therefore $\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{AG}{AC}=\frac{EG}{BC}=\frac{EG}{CD}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
since $EG\parallel BD$,\\
therefore $\triangle EFG \sim \triangle DFC$,\\
therefore $\frac{EG}{CD}=\frac{GF}{CF}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
therefore $CF=2GF$,\\
therefore $AG=CG=3GF$,\\
therefore $AF=AG+CF=4GF$,\\
therefore $AC=2CG=6GF$,\\
therefore $\frac{AF}{AC}=\frac{4GF}{6GF}=\boxed{\frac{2}{3}}$.
